newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares closed mixed, tech stocks shine.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares closed mixed, tech stocks shine.

text.p: Singapore shares closed mixed on Friday, but technology stocks powered the electronics index up six percent to a new high of 159.13 before easing near the close.

The rally in hi-tech stocks was sparked by Venture Maufacturing's launch of a new multi-media software. Venture shares soared to an intra-day high of Singapore $7.10 before easing to close at S$6.85, up S$1.70 in active volume of more than 4.4 million units.
"Tech stocks were not really moving in the morning but after the Venture news, everything shot up," said a broker with a Singapore firm.
Bucking the trend was Creative Technology, which slumped S$2 to end at S$34.50 on concerns that the company's profit would be hit by Venture's new product.
But analysts said the jury was still out on the actual impact on Creative, which is expected to release a strong set of results for 1996/97 financial year ended June 30 on Tuesday.
"We are still positive on Creative and we do not see Venture posing a strong threat so soon," said an analyst with a U.S. brokerage. Analysts also said the two firms have different market niches.
But Creative's fall pulled the electronics index off its high to end at 157.69, up 7.09 points.
Topping the actives list was Gul Technologies, which ended at a new high of S$0.925, up 7.5 cents with more than 11 million traded.

Chinese drug firm Tianjin Zhongxin was also active in the afternoon session and closed unchanged at US$1.61. "It looks like the profit taking in this stock has been well absorbed and it should head up again next week," a broker said.
Keppel Corp managed break its three-day losing steak to end five cents up at S$6.50 with more than 8.9 million shares traded.
